transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Morales (Redwood SE); Samira Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Singh (VP Procurement, Nexus Health); Marcus Li (Security); Rosa Alvarez (Legal Counsel); Jon Park (CTO); Ellen Frost (Finance)

Summary (auto): kickoff to align on procurement gates, security artifacts, and pricing for pilot and production. Next: share docs, schedule pilot checklist, deliver MSA redline draft.

00:00:00 - Avery (Redwood): hey everybody thanks for joining, we'll wait a minute for people to hop in, appreciate it
00:00:12 - Priya (Nexus): thanks, yep we've got most of the team here on our end, hi all
00:01:05 - Avery: quick agenda. we want to cover the MSA/DPA expectations, billing acceptance process on your side, any FedRAMP-ish controls that alter scope, and then technical prerequisites for the pilot. diego will jump into the technical ask. sound right?
00:01:26 - Jon (Nexus): yep fine by me. also would like an estimate for dedicated pricing since we may need steady throughput for some clinical workloads
00:02:10 - Diego (Redwood): cool, i can do an initial delta. quick note — when you say fedramp, do you mean full fedramp authorization or a gap assessment to get you started? there's different paths.
00:02:33 - Marcus (Nexus): good question. our compliance team is looking for a fedramp pathway: initial gap assessment and then options to accelerate via dedicated private deployment, potentially a partner-hosted fedramp boundary. not expecting redwood to be the authorizing party but need the docs and controls mapping.
00:03:05 - Rosa (Nexus Legal): and from legal, we need to understand vendor subprocessor list, encryption at rest key ownership, and indemnity/limitation caps — those are primary sticking points for our counsel.
00:03:30 - Avery: understood. we'll outline our subprocessor list and KMS options — we have customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. for hosted we use an HSM-backed KMS but we can provide key-separation patterns.
00:04:10 - Ellen (Finance): can you also call out billing acceptance? our finance policy requires a test invoice and verification cycle before we let recurring payments flow. we usually do a one-month trial invoice, confirm fields, then approve.
00:04:37 - Samira (Redwood CSM): we can stand up a test billing tenant and generate a draft invoice. we do need to understand your required invoice line items (po number, cost center, project code).
00:05:05 - Priya: our gating docs include PO number, cost center, and a statement of work reference. procurement will need the MSA to reflect those.
00:05:30 - Diego: on the technical side for pilot: network egress ranges, VPC peering or private link preferences, and KMS integration. for Dedicated we support customer VPC + cross-account role. for Private on-prem we have an air-gapped option but that adds lead time.
00:06:12 - Marcus: latency SLOs matter for inference — we need 95th percentile below 200ms for standard gen tasks; can you confirm expected p95 for model X under dedicated GPU pool?
00:06:40 - Diego: we have benchmark numbers but they're model/seq-length dependent. for smaller context and our optimized kernels p95 on dedicated with appropriate instance sizing is typically ~120–250ms; we'll provide a model-specific table.
00:07:22 - Jon: also curious about KV cache behavior, we don't want cold-start spikes affecting service level.
00:07:45 - Diego: we do prefix caching and an active KV cache across warm instances; occasionally watch for cache churn on small workloads — it's, uh, K-V cash in some transcripts i know gets misheard — but we'll give the cache-hit metrics.
00:08:20 - Rosa: circling back to legal, can you clarify data retention and deletion procedures? we need 30-day deletion guarantees for PHI-derived transient vectors, at minimum.
00:08:41 - Avery: for Hosted we have configurable retention policies and a deletion API for customer data; Dedicated/Private gives you stronger guarantees since you control storage lifecycle. we'll supply the DPA appendix mapping to HIPAA/FedRAMP controls.
00:09:10 - Priya: timeline question — procurement typically needs legal sign-off plus finance for a pilot to be billable. if we get the MSA redline by next week, is a two-week review window reasonable?
00:09:34 - Rosa: yes that matches our schedule, but we'll flag any high-impact indemnity sections early.
00:09:50 - Avery: we'll put a redline-friendly version that calls out the critical DPA/indemnity pieces in summary.
00:10:20 - Ellen: on billing: are you able to produce invoices with custom cost centers mapped? we need CSV extracts and billing export for our internal chargeback.
00:10:36 - Samira: yes, we can provide exportable billing csvs and a billing api. i'll include sample fields.
00:11:05 - Priya: procurement also asks about price escalators — do you have a standard annual increase or is it locked for the term?
00:11:23 - Avery: our standard reserved capacity has a flat-rate term but hosted tiers may include usage escalators; we'll provide a T&Cs excerpt and a sample calculation for 12-month and 36-month terms.
00:12:00 - Marcus: security question: does Redwood support customer-managed keys in the dedicated contract and do you provide HSM-backed attestations?
00:12:20 - Diego: yes for Dedicated and Private we can integrate with customer KMS (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) with CMEK. HSM attestations are available as part of our enterprise package; we'll send the attestation template.
00:13:05 - Rosa: and how about audit logs? we need immutable audit logs for API access and admin changes retained for 365 days minimum for FedRAMP.
00:13:24 - Diego: default retention is 90 days for hosted, but for enterprise we can extend to 365 and provide log export hooks to your SIEM. that will go into the private/dedicated appendix.
00:14:02 - Priya: procurement gating: we need to see risk scoring on your side, subprocessor maps, and incident response SLA. do you have a high-level risk assessment?
00:14:25 - Avery: yes we'll include a short risk addendum and our incident response SLA. we have an incident tiering model; P1 escalations have 30-minute ack times for enterprise tenants.
00:15:05 - Jon: timeline again — assuming we get docs by friday, what benchmarking do we need to run for the pilot?
00:15:23 - Diego: recommended pilot steps: run 3 typical inference workloads, measure p50/p95 latency, token cost per request, and throughput under parallel clients. we'll provide a benchmarking spreadsheet.
00:16:05 - Priya: any third-party certifications we can lean on for procurement? you mentioned SOC2; do you have FedRAMP in process?
00:16:22 - Avery: we have SOC2 Type II and ISO coverage for some components; FedRAMP is not an active authorization yet but we maintain control mappings and we can do a gap assessment to map our controls to FedRAMP requirements.
00:16:55 - Rosa: that helps; we will ask for the control mapping doc.
00:17:20 - Ellen: on invoicing cadence, do you support net-30?
00:17:32 - Avery: yes net-30 is standard for enterprise contract, but we can negotiate payment terms in the SOW.
00:18:10 - Samira: quick note — for the pilot we recommend hosted with VPC peering, then transition to Dedicated for production if you need a fedramp boundary; that path shortens time to value.
00:18:45 - Marcus: can you clarify data residency for backups? backups should be in our region only.
00:18:58 - Diego: regional backups are possible for Dedicated and Private; hosted has region options but some shared components are global. we'll mark those clearly.
00:19:35 - Priya: procurement prefers a clause that requires vendor to notify of subcontractor changes 30 days in advance. acceptable?
00:19:50 - Rosa: also seeking a clause for annual tabletop exercises with vendor for incident response.
00:20:05 - Avery: we can add a 30-day notice for subprocessor changes and include tabletop cadence in enterprise support addendum.
00:20:40 - Jon: do you have an escrow option for critical code or model weights?
00:20:56 - Avery: we don't typically escrow model weights; we can discuss an escrow for configuration and critical deployment artifacts in high-assurance deals.
00:21:30 - Priya: procurement needs a completed vendor intake form — we'll send it after the call. can redwood fill vendor-specific fields?
00:21:45 - Samira: yes we'll populate it and return within 48 hours of receiving.
00:22:12 - Diego: technical note — for the pilot to validate latency, we'll need a small test dataset and maybe a representative prompt set; also, if you're using PHI, ensure we have a BAA in place.
00:22:40 - Marcus: yes PHI is in scope for some workloads, we will require a BAA.
00:23:05 - Rosa: BAA will be a gating legal doc, we won't sign the MSA without it.
00:23:32 - Avery: understoood — we'll prepare a BAA appendix.
00:24:10 - Ellen: procurement asks for W-9 and vendor remittance info for initial onboarding.
00:24:25 - Avery: i'll have finance send a W-9 and vendor setup guide.
00:25:00 - Priya: any client references in healthcare you can share? it's helpful for procurement to see similar profiles.
00:25:15 - Avery: yes we can provide two anonymized references and a short case study showing dedicated deployment for clinical ingestion workloads.
00:25:50 - Rosa: legal wants to propose a clause limiting onboarding access to only named engineers, to reduce blast radius. is role-based access control available?
00:26:10 - Diego: yes RBAC is supported with SSO/SAML and scoped roles; for Dedicated you can map to your identity provider and limit admin rights.
00:26:50 - Priya: perfect. procurement will include an approval step for SSO integration in the SOW.
00:27:20 - Avery: ok let's quickly surface the likely redline hotspots: indemnity caps, data deletion timelines, export control language, and subprocessor change notice. we'll annotate those in the redline.
00:27:45 - Rosa: indemnity — we prefer a mutual indemnity for data breaches due to negligence, and a capped liability aligned to the contract value. we'll flag target language in our vendor form.
00:28:10 - Avery: we'll propose compromise language; we'll call out the enterprise template and show options.
00:28:45 - Diego: another technical item — if you plan to use any private models or on-prem weights, that impacts deployment time and licensing.
00:29:10 - Jon: we may bring a fine-tuned model; can you support bringing our weights for hosting?
00:29:25 - Diego: yes, we have a supported workflow for bringing your own model artifacts; for on-prem there are extra validation steps. we'll list those.
00:29:55 - Priya: procurement rate-limits: we need to know who signs off on exceptions — is that AE or legal?
00:30:12 - Avery: major legal exceptions go to legal; pricing exceptions go through AE+rev ops. I'll connect rev ops if needed.
00:30:45 - Samira: operationally, account enablement for pilot takes ~3 business days after we get vendor form and finance set-up.
00:31:12 - Ellen: do you require a PO to start the pilot?
00:31:23 - Priya: our procurement prefers a small PO for pilot billing acceptance, yes.
00:31:40 - Avery: we can accept a PO, or run on credit for short pilots; will confirm details in the follow-up.
00:32:05 - Marcus: regarding incident SLA, what is the escalation path and contact method?
00:32:20 - Diego: P1 via pager and email with 30-minute response; we have a dedicated enterprise slack channel if you want real-time updates.
00:32:55 - Rosa: legal wants to retain the right to audit once per year. is on-site audit support available?
00:33:12 - Avery: yes remote audits are typically supported; on-site audits can be arranged for enterprise deals with notice.
00:33:45 - Priya: procurement note: our approval timeline is ~4 weeks post-delivery of docs if no material redlines.
00:34:00 - Avery: noted. we'll aim to deliver the MSA redline and technical attachments by 2026-03-28 to meet that cadence.
00:34:35 - Diego: i'll prepare the benchmarking spreadsheet and template run instructions; we'll also include a sample set of model configs.
00:34:58 - Priya: great. One small ask: show the invoice sample fields in your follow-up so finance can validate auto-import to our AP system.
00:35:18 - Samira: on it — sample invoice will be attached.
00:35:45 - Jon: can we get a short note on SLA credits and how they're calculated?
00:35:58 - Avery: yes SLA credit table will be included in the appendix.
00:36:30 - Marcus: any concerns about data flow to third countries for monitoring/ops?
00:36:45 - Diego: we can restrict egress to region for Dedicated; hosted may have ops telemetry routed to global endpoints but we can provide assurances and a config that minimizes cross-border transfers.
00:37:20 - Rosa: will your DPA include special terms for PHI?
00:37:32 - Avery: yes BAA appendix will be provided; we'll mark PHI-specific retention and handling.
00:38:00 - Priya: okay quick recap of deliverables?
00:38:10 - Avery: redline-ready MSA + DPA appendix; SOC2 report + control mapping; pricing matrix for hosted vs dedicated; pilot benchmarking spreadsheet; sample invoice; vendor setup docs + W-9.
00:38:35 - Rosa: please flag any non-negotiable settlement items in your redline so counsel can triage.
00:38:50 - Avery: will do.
00:39:15 - Ellen: finance will expect an initial PO for pilot; we'll send procurement's vendor intake within 24 hours.
00:39:30 - Priya: timeline review: docs by 3/28, procurement review 3/29-4/9, pilot week of 4/6 or 4/13 pending provisioning.
00:39:50 - Diego: provisioning estimate — 3 business days for hosted pilot, 7–14 for dedicated staging depending on instance availability.
00:40:12 - Jon: any blockers you anticipate?
00:40:25 - Avery: only blocker might be indemnity cap negotiations or a FedRAMP scope increase; we'll surface those early.
00:40:50 - Samira: i'll open the pilot ticket and create the billing tenant once W-9 and vendor form are done.
00:41:15 - Priya: thanks team.
00:41:25 - Rosa: one more legal quirk — we need retention on logs to be specified and a deletion certificate when requested.
00:41:45 - Diego: we can provide deletion confirmations for customer data and attach export.
00:42:10 - Avery: ok closing notes: we'll send everything as actioned; next call would be a legal redline review with Rosa and procurement in roughly two weeks.
00:42:35 - Priya: schedule that once you've sent docs.
00:42:50 - Avery: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a single email that contains links to the artifacts and next steps.
00:43:10 - Meeting end

Notes on transcription quality: some technical terms were transcribed inconsistently (e.g., "KV cache" as "K-V cash"). occasional crosstalk at 00:25.

End of transcript.
